error_modes.label: MISSION PROFILE AND OBJECTIVES AS LEADER

texts.0: SP, due to a threat present in the minimum threat set but not identified in the planning phase, did not determine the mission profile and did not set objectives according to the experience level of the formation and the difficulty level of the mission. The profile brought to the briefing room had no sequence of events, no working area allocation and no objective assigned to the wingman, and the forecast weather at the recovery time was left unaddressed. IP had to suspend the brief, build the profile and set the objectives before the formation could be released.
texts.1: SP, due to mission planning that did not address the forecast weather at the recovery time, did not determine a complete mission profile and set objectives that did not match the experience level of the wingman. Four items of the profile were entered only after IP named each of them in turn, and the objectives were rewritten twice on IP direction. The plan reached the lower limit of the standard by verbal prompting alone and delayed the brief by about fifteen minutes.
texts.2: SP, due to a currency shortfall that was not addressed at the start of the planning phase, first set objectives above the level the formation could fly on that sortie. SP recognized the mismatch while reviewing the profile against the syllabus event, reduced the objectives and reallocated the working area before the brief opened, without IP intervention. The profile presented then covered the full sequence of events with objectives matched to the formation.
texts.3: SP determined the mission profile and set the objectives according to the experience level of the formation and the difficulty level of the mission. The sequence of events, working area allocation, timings and the objective for each member were defined before the brief and required no correction by IP. The profile was consistent with the syllabus event throughout.
texts.4: SP produced a mission profile of exceptional quality, with the sequence of events, area allocation, timings and individual objectives built around the specific experience level of the wingman and the specific difficulty of the sortie. Every threat in the minimum threat set was addressed in the profile before the brief opened, with the mitigation already worked out. Deviations from the ideal profile were negligible.
texts.marginal: SP determined the mission profile and set objectives within standards, but the objectives were stated in general terms and gave the wingman no measurable target for the sortie, and the profile carried no margin for a delayed area entry. The trend is toward a profile that satisfies the requirement on paper while leaving the debriefing with nothing specific to measure. SP is expected to state objectives in measurable terms and to build usable margin into the profile on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP built the mission profile with the IP naming the sequence of events, the working area allocation and the objectives to be set for the formation. Building a complete mission profile from experience level and mission difficulty is a first exposure at this stage, so the sequence is not yet assembled without a cue. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to state objectives in measurable terms and build usable margin into the profile.
texts_at.1: SP, due to mission planning that left the forecast recovery weather unaddressed until it was raised, produced a profile with the objectives rewritten once before they matched the wingman's experience level, reaching the standard only at the edge of the time available. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to state objectives in measurable terms and build usable margin into the profile.
texts_at.2: SP, due to a currency shortfall not addressed at the start of planning, initially set objectives above the level the formation could fly on the sortie before recognizing the mismatch and reducing them without prompting, ahead of the brief. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to state objectives in measurable terms and build usable margin into the profile.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief gap in checking the sortie against the syllabus event before the profile was finalized, determined the mission profile and set the objectives according to the experience level of the formation, with the sequence of events and area allocation defined before the brief. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to state objectives in measurable terms and build usable margin into the profile.

texts_above.1: SP produced the mission profile with the objectives matched to the experience level of the formation, completing the sequence of events after the forecast weather was raised on a verbal call from the IP. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP initially set objectives above the level the formation could fly on the sortie before recognizing the mismatch and reducing them without prompting, presenting a complete profile before the brief opened. Checking the objectives against the syllabus event before the first draft, rather than after, would remove that revision. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to good mission-profile completeness discipline.
texts_above.3: SP determined the mission profile and set the objectives according to the experience level of the formation and the difficulty of the mission, with the sequence of events, area allocation and timings defined before the brief and requiring no correction. The profile is already complete and consistent with the syllabus event; only the smallest further margin remains. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to very good mission-profile completeness discipline.
texts_above.4: SP produced a mission profile built around the wingman's specific experience level and the sortie's specific difficulty, with every threat in the minimum threat set already addressed and its mitigation worked out before the brief opened. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to excellent mission-profile completeness discipline.

error_modes.label: DIRECTIVES FOR MISSION PROFILE AND BRIEFING GUIDE BOOK COMPLIANCE

texts.0: SP, as leader, did not execute the mission briefing according to the Briefing Guide Book and did not give solid directives for the mission profile. Whole sections of the guide covering join-up, lost wingman and knock-it-off call standards were omitted, and the directives given for the profile were open to more than one reading. IP had to stop the briefing and cover the omitted sections before the formation stepped.
texts.1: SP, as leader, executed the briefing in an order that did not follow the Briefing Guide Book and gave directives that left the wingman without a defined action for two events of the profile. Both sections were covered only after IP named them, and the directives were restated on IP prompting. The briefing met the lower limit of the standard by verbal prompting alone and ran about twenty minutes past its planned end.
texts.2: SP, as leader, initially covered the mission profile without giving the airspeed and altitude directives for the transit segment. SP identified the omission on reaching the next section of the Briefing Guide Book, returned to the profile and gave the missing directives before continuing, without IP intervention. The remaining sections of the guide were then delivered in the published order.
texts.3: SP executed the mission briefing according to the Briefing Guide Book and gave solid directives for the mission profile. Each section of the guide was covered in the published order and every phase of the profile was tied to a directive that admitted a single interpretation. No section required completion by IP.
texts.4: SP delivered a briefing of exceptional quality, covering every section of the Briefing Guide Book and supporting each phase of the profile with a directive stated in terms of airspeed, position and responsibility. Contingencies raised from the floor were answered with directives already prepared in the planning phase. The formation left the briefing room with no point of the profile undefined.
texts.marginal: SP executed the briefing according to the Briefing Guide Book within standards, but several directives were given as intentions rather than as instructions, and two sections were read from the guide without being related to the profile of the day. The trend is toward a briefing that discharges the format while leaving the wingman to infer what is actually required. SP is expected to convert each section of the guide into a specific directive for the flown profile on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP delivered the mission briefing with the IP naming each section of the Briefing Guide Book and the directive it requires. Converting a section of the guide into a specific directive for the profile is a first exposure at this stage, so the directive is not yet stated without a cue. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to convert each section of the guide into a specific directive for the flown profile.
texts_at.1: SP, due to a briefing order that did not follow the Briefing Guide Book, covered two events of the profile only after returning to them, with the briefing meeting the standard only at the edge of the time allotted. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to convert each section of the guide into a specific directive for the flown profile.
texts_at.2: SP, due to an initial pass through the profile that omitted the airspeed and altitude directives for the transit segment, identified the omission on reaching the next section of the guide, returned to the profile and gave the missing directives before continuing, without prompting. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to convert each section of the guide into a specific directive for the flown profile.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief gap before the transit-segment directives were stated, executed the mission briefing according to the Briefing Guide Book, giving solid directives for the mission profile with each section covered in the published order. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to convert each section of the guide into a specific directive for the flown profile.

texts_above.1: SP delivered the mission briefing according to the Briefing Guide Book, returning to state the missing transit-segment directives after they were named by the IP. The result is above the code required for this Training Section at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP omitted the airspeed and altitude directives for the transit segment on the first pass before identifying the gap on reaching the next section, returning to the profile and completing the directives without prompting. Cross-checking each section against the profile as it is delivered, rather than afterward, would remove that return. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to sound briefing-directive specificity.
texts_above.3: SP executed the mission briefing according to the Briefing Guide Book and gave solid directives for the mission profile, with each section covered in the published order and every phase tied to a directive admitting a single interpretation. The directives already admit only one reading; only the smallest sequencing gap remains to close. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to sure-handed briefing-directive specificity.
texts_above.4: SP delivered a briefing covering every section of the Briefing Guide Book with each phase of the profile supported by a directive stated in terms of airspeed, position and responsibility, answering contingencies from prepared material. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to exceptional briefing-directive specificity.

error_modes.label: CONTROL OF THE BRIEFING AND DEBRIEFING PROCESS

texts.0: SP, as leader, did not have control of the briefing process. The session was taken over by questions from the floor within the first minutes, the planned order was abandoned and about half of the profile was never reached before the time available ran out. IP had to take control of the room and complete the process.
texts.1: SP, as leader, lost control of the briefing at three points where the discussion moved off the profile, and did not bring it back until IP directed it. The remaining sections were then covered against the clock, with the last two rushed. The process was completed to the lower limit of the standard only through IP prompting and overran the allotted time by about fifteen minutes.
texts.2: SP, as leader, allowed a discussion of a secondary point to run past its place in the briefing sequence. SP recognized within about a minute that the profile had not been reached, closed the discussion, deferred the point to the debriefing and returned to the planned order, without IP intervention. The briefing was completed within the time available.
texts.3: SP had control of the briefing and debriefing process throughout. Discussion was taken at the points where it belonged, closed once the point had been answered and deferred when it fell outside the profile of the day, and both sessions finished within the time allotted. The formation was never in doubt about which part of the process was in progress.
texts.4: SP exercised exceptional control of the briefing and debriefing process, holding the planned order while still drawing every member into the discussion at the point where their input mattered. Questions were answered without loss of the thread and the session finished ahead of the time allotted with all content covered. No part of the process required redirection.
texts.marginal: SP had control of the briefing and debriefing process within standards, but the pace was set by the clock rather than by the content, and two discussions were closed before the wingman had finished the point being made. The trend is toward control maintained at the cost of the exchange the process exists to produce. SP is expected to hold the order of the session while leaving room for the formation to contribute on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP ran the briefing with the IP calling the point at which a discussion had moved off the planned order. Holding control of the briefing sequence while a discussion is in progress is a first exposure at this stage, so the order is not yet held without a cue. The maneuver is being introduced at this point of the syllabus, so no independent standard is required yet. SP is expected to hold the order of the session while leaving room for the formation to contribute.
texts_at.1: SP, due to a discussion allowed to run past its place in the briefing sequence, brought the session back to the profile only at the edge of the time available, with the last sections compressed. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to hold the order of the session while leaving room for the formation to contribute.
texts_at.2: SP, due to a secondary discussion allowed to run past its place in the sequence, closed the discussion within about a minute of recognizing the profile had not been reached, deferred the point to the debriefing and returned to the planned order without prompting. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to hold the order of the session while leaving room for the formation to contribute.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief overrun of a discussion before it was closed, had control of the briefing and debriefing process throughout, taking discussion at the points where it belonged and closing it once the point had been answered. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to hold the order of the session while leaving room for the formation to contribute.

texts_above.1: SP held control of the briefing and debriefing process, bringing a discussion back to the planned order after it was raised by the IP. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus.
texts_above.2: SP let a secondary discussion run a little past its place in the sequence before recognizing within about a minute that the profile had not been reached, closing the discussion and returning to the planned order without prompting. Setting a time limit on secondary discussion before it starts would remove that brief overrun. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to solid briefing-process control technique.
texts_above.3: SP had control of the briefing and debriefing process throughout, taking discussion at the points where it belonged and closing it once answered, with both sessions finishing within the time allotted. The control of the sequence is already consistent through both sessions; only the smallest timing margin remains. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to well-developed briefing-process control technique.
texts_above.4: SP held control of the briefing and debriefing process while still drawing every member into the discussion at the point their input mattered, finishing ahead of the time allotted with all content covered. error_modes.label: CRM COMPREHENSION BY ALL FORMATION MEMBERS BEFORE BRIEFING COMPLETION

texts.0: SP, due to lack of communication of the recognized difference to the other members, did not make sure that the CRM content was comprehensible to all formation members before the briefing was completed. No comprehension check was made at any point, and two members left the room with different understandings of the lost wingman procedure and of who held responsibility for lookout during the transit. IP had to reopen the briefing and re-establish the common picture before the formation stepped.
texts.1: SP, due to an indirect hint instead of a direct statement of the responsibilities, did not confirm that the CRM content was completely comprehensible to all members and closed the briefing on a general question that drew no answer. The comprehension check was carried out only after IP directed that each member be asked individually, and it revealed one item that had not been understood. The requirement was met at its lower limit and only through that prompting.
texts.2: SP, due to failure to pass a required confirmation at the briefed point, initially closed the CRM section without checking that the knock-it-off call standards had been understood. SP recognized the omission before moving to the next section, returned to the point and confirmed the standards with each member individually, without IP intervention. All members left the briefing with the same understanding of the calls.
texts.3: SP made sure that the CRM content was completely comprehensible to all formation members and confirmed it before the briefing was completed. Each member was asked directly about the responsibilities, the call standards and the contingencies, and every answer was correct. The formation left the room with a single common picture of the mission.
texts.4: SP ensured comprehension of the CRM content to an exceptional standard, checking understanding at the end of each section rather than only at the close, and using specific scenario questions in place of a general invitation to ask. Where an answer was incomplete, SP restated the point and confirmed it again before moving on. No element of the mission was left with more than one interpretation.
texts.marginal: SP confirmed comprehension of the CRM content within standards, but the check was made as a single question to the formation as a whole and only one member answered. The trend is toward a confirmation that records agreement without testing it. SP is expected to check understanding member by member and against specific mission events on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP checked comprehension of the CRM content with the IP directing that each member be asked individually. Confirming comprehension of the CRM content member by member is a first exposure at this stage, so the check is not yet made without a cue. Performance is consistent with a first exposure at this point of the syllabus, where the Training Section still provides assistance. SP is expected to check understanding member by member and against specific mission events.
texts_at.1: SP, due to an indirect hint rather than a direct statement of the responsibilities, confirmed comprehension only after being directed to ask each member individually, meeting the standard at the edge of what the closing question allowed. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to check understanding member by member and against specific mission events.
texts_at.2: SP, due to a comprehension section initially closed before checking that the knock-it-off call standards had been understood, recognized the omission before moving to the next section, returned to the point and confirmed the standards with each member individually, without prompting. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to check understanding member by member and against specific mission events.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief gap before the individual confirmation was completed, made sure the CRM content was completely comprehensible to all formation members and confirmed it before the briefing was completed, asking each member directly. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to check understanding member by member and against specific mission events.

texts_above.1: SP confirmed comprehension of the CRM content member by member, asking each one individually after the requirement was raised by the IP. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP initially closed the CRM section before checking that the knock-it-off call standards had been understood, then recognized the omission before the next section, returned to the point and confirmed the standards with each member individually, without prompting. Confirming each item as the section closes, rather than moving past it, would remove that return. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady CRM comprehension-check discipline.
texts_above.3: SP made sure the CRM content was completely comprehensible to all formation members and confirmed it before the briefing was completed, asking each member directly about responsibilities, call standards and contingencies. The confirmation already reaches every member individually; only the smallest sequencing gap remains. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to consistently accurate CRM comprehension-check discipline.

error_modes.label: ALTERNATIVE WAYS OF EXECUTION AND DECISION POINTS IN THE PLAN

texts.0: SP, as leader, did not plan the mission profile taking under consideration alternative ways of execution. No alternative was prepared for a closed working area, for a weather deterioration or for a ground abort of the wingman, and no decision point or divert criterion was named anywhere in the profile. IP had to build the contingency plan and state the divert criteria before the formation was released.
texts.1: SP, as leader, planned a single way of executing the profile and left both the alternative for the second working area and the criteria for using it undefined. The alternative profile and the divert criteria were produced only after IP named each one in turn. The plan reached the lower limit of the standard by prompting alone and delayed the release of the formation.
texts.2: SP, as leader, first presented a profile with one line of execution and no decision point for the weather deterioration that had been forecast. SP identified the gap while comparing the forecast against the planned recovery time, added an alternative working area and a named decision point for the recovery, and briefed both, without IP intervention. The plan then covered the forecast condition.
texts.3: SP planned the mission profile taking under consideration alternative ways of execution. An alternative was defined for the working area, for the recovery and for a ground abort of one member, each tied to a named decision point and to stated criteria. The formation was briefed on all alternatives before the briefing was completed.
texts.4: SP produced contingency planning of exceptional quality, with an alternative for every phase of the profile, a named decision point for each and the criteria for choosing between them stated in terms the wingman could apply independently. The alternatives were themselves cross-checked against fuel and against the recovery time. No part of the profile depended on a single line of execution.
texts.marginal: SP planned alternative ways of execution within standards, but the alternatives were described in outline and the criteria for selecting them were left to be decided airborne. The trend is toward contingency planning that exists in the brief without being usable under workload. SP is expected to attach specific criteria and a named decision point to each alternative on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP planned the mission profile with the IP naming each alternative and the decision point it needs. Attaching a named decision point and criteria to an alternative is a first exposure at this stage, so the plan is not yet built without a cue. The Training Section still expects IP assistance for this maneuver at this point. SP is expected to attach specific criteria and a named decision point to each alternative.
texts_at.1: SP, due to a plan built around a single line of execution before the alternative was worked out, produced the alternative profile and divert criteria only after each was named in turn, reaching the standard at the edge of the time available before release. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to attach specific criteria and a named decision point to each alternative.
texts_at.2: SP, due to a first profile with one line of execution and no decision point for the forecast weather deterioration, identified the gap while comparing the forecast against the planned recovery time, added an alternative working area and a named decision point, and briefed both, without prompting. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to attach specific criteria and a named decision point to each alternative.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief gap before the decision point for the forecast condition was added, planned the mission profile taking under consideration alternative ways of execution, with an alternative defined for the working area and the recovery, each tied to a named decision point. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to attach specific criteria and a named decision point to each alternative.

texts_above.1: SP planned the mission profile with an alternative way of execution, adding the decision point for the forecast weather after it was raised by the IP. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP presented a first profile with one line of execution and no decision point for the forecast weather deterioration before identifying the gap, adding an alternative working area and a named decision point, and briefing both without prompting. Building the decision point in alongside the first line of execution, rather than after, would remove that addition. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to dependable contingency-planning completeness.
texts_above.3: SP planned the mission profile taking under consideration alternative ways of execution, with an alternative defined for the working area, the recovery and a ground abort, each tied to a named decision point and stated criteria. The alternatives already carry a named decision point each; only the smallest further margin remains. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to notably good contingency-planning completeness.
texts_above.4: SP produced contingency planning with an alternative for every phase of the profile, a named decision point for each and criteria the wingman could apply independently, cross-checked against fuel and the recovery time. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to superior contingency-planning completeness.

error_modes.label: DEBRIEFING EXECUTION AND ANALYSIS OF OBJECTIVES COMPLETION

texts.0: SP, as leader, did not execute the mission debriefing according to the Briefing Guide and did not cover the faults of the formation members. The session consisted of a general statement that the mission had gone well, no objective was assessed against what had been set in the brief and no fault was named. IP had to conduct the debriefing in full.
texts.1: SP, as leader, executed a debriefing that followed the Briefing Guide only in part and covered two of the six faults observed during the sortie. The remaining faults and the analysis of objectives completion were addressed only after IP identified each in turn. The debriefing met the lower limit of the standard through that prompting and left the wingman without a ranked list of points to work on.
texts.2: SP, as leader, opened the debriefing on the formation faults without first analyzing completion of the objectives set in the brief. SP recognized the departure from the Briefing Guide within the first minutes, returned to the objectives, assessed each against the standard set and then continued with the faults, without IP intervention. All points of the sortie were covered.
texts.3: SP executed the mission debriefing according to the Briefing Guide, covering the faults of each formation member and analyzing completion of the objectives set in the brief. Each fault was stated with its cause and its effect on the profile, and each objective was assessed against the standard defined before the sortie. The session closed with agreed points to work on.
texts.4: SP delivered a debriefing of exceptional quality, assessing every objective against the standard set in the brief, tracing each fault to its cause and ranking the points by their effect on the mission. The wingman was drawn into the analysis of their own faults rather than being told them, and the session produced specific and achievable corrections. Nothing observed during the sortie was left unaddressed.
texts.marginal: SP executed the debriefing according to the Briefing Guide within standards, but the faults were listed without being tied to their causes and the analysis of objectives was reduced to a completed or not completed statement. The trend is toward a debriefing that records the sortie without improving the next one. SP is expected to state the cause and the effect of each fault and to measure each objective against the briefed standard on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP ran the debriefing with the IP naming each objective to be analyzed before the formation faults were covered. Opening the debriefing on objectives completion before the faults is a first exposure at this stage, so the sequence is not yet followed without a cue. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to state the cause and the effect of each fault and measure each objective against the briefed standard.
texts_at.1: SP, due to a debriefing opened directly on the formation faults rather than on objectives completion, reached the analysis of objectives only after the sequence prescribed by the Briefing Guide had already been raised, meeting the standard at the edge of the time remaining. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to state the cause and the effect of each fault and measure each objective against the briefed standard.
texts_at.2: SP, due to a debriefing opened on the formation faults without first analyzing completion of the briefed objectives, recognized the departure from the Briefing Guide within the first minutes, returned to the objectives, assessed each against the standard set and then continued with the faults, without prompting. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to state the cause and the effect of each fault and measure each objective against the briefed standard.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief departure from the guide's order before it was corrected, executed the mission debriefing according to the Briefing Guide, covering the faults of each formation member and analyzing completion of the objectives set in the brief. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to state the cause and the effect of each fault and measure each objective against the briefed standard.

texts_above.1: SP ran the debriefing according to the Briefing Guide, returning to the analysis of objectives after the sequence was raised by the IP. The result is above the code required for this Training Section at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP opened the debriefing on the formation faults without first analyzing completion of the objectives, then recognized the departure from the Briefing Guide within the first minutes, returned to the objectives and continued with the faults, without prompting. Opening on the objectives before the faults, in the guide's own order, would remove that return. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to assured debrief root-cause sequencing.
texts_above.3: SP executed the mission debriefing according to the Briefing Guide, covering the faults of each formation member and analyzing completion of the objectives, with each fault stated with its cause and effect on the profile. The sequencing already follows the guide closely; only the smallest departure from it remains. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to precise debrief root-cause sequencing.

error_modes.label: WINGMAN ATTENDANCE AND ASSISTANCE TO THE LEADER

texts.0: SP, due to an authority gradient that suppressed the upward input, did not attend the briefing flow as a participant and did not assist the leader in assessing the mission elements. The NOTAMs affecting the recovery airfield had been read by SP before the session and were never passed to the leader, and the formation planned against an airfield with a closed runway. IP had to stop the process and hand the information across.
texts.1: SP, due to reluctance to raise a point perceived as the leader prerogative, followed the briefing flow without offering the meteorological and alternate airfield data that had been prepared. The information reached the leader only after IP asked SP directly what had been found during planning. The assistance requirement was met at its lower limit and only through that prompting.
texts.2: SP, due to deference to the leader that initially replaced own assessment, held back a discrepancy noticed between the briefed alternate airfield and the current NOTAMs. SP recognized within about a minute that the point had to be passed, raised it at the next break in the briefing flow and the alternate was changed, without IP intervention. The formation planned against current information.
texts.3: SP attended the briefing and debriefing flow and assisted the leader in assessing the mission elements. NOTAMs, meteorological data and alternate airfield status had been checked before the session and were offered at the points where they bore on the plan. The leader received every item needed without having to ask for it.
texts.4: SP supported the leader to an exceptional standard, arriving with NOTAMs, weather and alternate airfield status already compared against the planned profile and the recovery time. Each item was offered at the moment it bore on a decision, stated briefly and without displacing the leader authority over the plan. The leader was able to plan against complete and current information throughout.
texts.marginal: SP attended the briefing flow and assisted the leader within standards, but the input was given only when asked for and two items relevant to the recovery were held until the leader raised the subject. The trend is toward assistance that waits to be requested rather than being offered when it matters. SP is expected to pass mission-relevant information at the point it bears on the plan on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP attended the briefing flow with the IP asking directly what had been found during planning. Offering mission-relevant information without being asked is a first exposure at this stage, so the assistance is not yet given without a cue. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to pass mission-relevant information at the point it bears on the plan.

None of the three assessment areas was addressed: the index of thermal stress and the bird status for the working period, the risk carried by the formation profile itself, and the currency and fatigue state of the wingman were all left unexamined. The assessment reached the lower limit of the standard by verbal prompting alone.
texts.2: SP, due to an initial assessment that weighed training benefit without weighing the risk against it, first accepted a profile whose low level segment coincided with the peak bird activity period. error_modes.label: TIME SPENT ON S.O.P MATERIAL INSTEAD OF THE HOW TO OF THE MISSION

texts.0: SP, as leader, spent the briefing reading S.O.P material that every formation member is required to hold committed to memory and never reached the how to of the mission. Standard elements that could have been briefed as standard consumed the whole session, and the profile of the day, the objectives and the contingencies were not covered at all. IP had to stop the briefing and brief the mission itself before the formation stepped.
texts.1: SP, as leader, gave about two thirds of the briefing to S.O.P material and reached the how to of the mission only in the last minutes. The profile was compressed and the objectives were covered only after IP directed that they be briefed. The session met the lower limit of the standard through that prompting and overran the time allotted by about twenty minutes.
texts.2: SP, as leader, opened the briefing by working through the standard start, taxi and takeoff procedures item by item although they are conducted in accordance with S.O.P. SP recognized after several minutes that the majority of the time was going to material already committed to memory, briefed the remaining standard elements as standard and moved to the how to of the profile, without IP intervention. The briefing finished within the time allotted with all mission content covered.
texts.3: SP briefed the elements conducted in accordance with S.O.P as standard and spent the majority of the session on the how to of the mission. The profile, the objectives and the standard used to measure successful performance were developed in detail, with only the departures from S.O.P called out. The briefing was clear, concise and finished within the time allotted.
texts.4: SP delivered a briefing of exceptional economy, disposing of the standard elements in a single statement and devoting the whole of the remaining time to how the mission would be flown. Each phase of the profile was briefed in terms of what each member does, sees and calls, and the departures from S.O.P were highlighted against the standard rather than read alongside it. The formation left with a detailed mental picture of the sortie and no time wasted.
texts.marginal: SP briefed the S.O.P elements as standard and covered the how to of the mission within standards, but about a third of the session was still given to procedures the formation holds committed to memory. The trend is toward a briefing that fills the time available rather than spending it where the mission is won. SP is expected to brief standard elements as standard and to convert the time recovered into detail on the profile on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP briefed the mission with the IP directing that the S.O.P material be covered as standard and time be moved to the how to of the profile. Recognizing which briefing material is already committed to memory is a first exposure at this stage, so the time allocation is not yet made without a cue. Performance is consistent with a first exposure at this point of the syllabus, where the Training Section still provides assistance. SP is expected to brief standard elements as standard and convert the time recovered into detail on the profile.
texts_at.1: SP, due to a briefing that reached the how to of the mission only in the last minutes, compressed the profile and covered the objectives only after being directed to brief them, overrunning the time allotted before the standard was met. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to brief standard elements as standard and convert the time recovered into detail on the profile.
texts_at.2: SP, due to an opening that worked through standard start, taxi and takeoff procedures item by item, recognized after several minutes that most of the time was going to material already committed to memory, briefing the remaining standard elements as standard and moving to the how to of the profile without prompting. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to brief standard elements as standard and convert the time recovered into detail on the profile.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief overrun on standard material before the shift to the how to of the profile, briefed the elements conducted in accordance with S.O.P as standard and spent the majority of the session on the how to of the mission, developing the profile and objectives in detail. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to brief standard elements as standard and convert the time recovered into detail on the profile.

texts_above.1: SP briefed the standard elements and the how to of the mission, moving to the profile after the objectives were directed to be briefed by the IP. The result is above the code required for this Training Section at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP worked through standard start, taxi and takeoff procedures item by item at first before recognizing after several minutes that most of the time was going to material already committed to memory, briefing the rest as standard and moving to the how to of the profile without prompting. Disposing of standard material in a single statement from the outset would remove that early item-by-item pass. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to competent briefing-time allocation discipline.
texts_above.3: SP briefed the elements conducted in accordance with S.O.P as standard and spent the majority of the session on the how to of the mission, with the profile, objectives and standard for measuring performance developed in detail. The time allocation already favors the how to of the mission; only the smallest further margin remains. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to disciplined briefing-time allocation discipline.
texts_above.4: SP disposed of the standard elements in a single statement and devoted the whole of the remaining time to how the mission would be flown, briefing each phase in terms of what each member does, sees and calls with no time wasted. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to faultless briefing-time allocation discipline.

error_modes.label: CREW BRIEFING TIME FOR INTER-COCKPIT RESPONSIBILITIES AND CREW COORDINATION

texts.0: SP, as briefer, allowed no time for the crews to brief inter-cockpit responsibilities, emergency procedures and crew coordination, and released the formation directly from the mass brief to the aircraft. Neither cockpit had agreed who flies, who works the radios or how control would be transferred in an emergency. IP had to recall the formation and have the crew briefings conducted before the step.
texts.1: SP, as briefer, allowed about two minutes for the crew briefings against the five minutes required as a minimum, and the emergency procedures and crew coordination items were left uncovered in one cockpit. The additional time was granted only after IP directed it, and the outstanding items were then briefed under time pressure. The requirement was met at its lower limit by that prompting alone.
texts.2: SP, as briefer, moved to release the formation without calling the crew briefing period. SP recognized before the members left the room that no time had been set aside, called the period, allowed the full five minutes and confirmed that inter-cockpit responsibilities and emergency procedures had been covered, without IP intervention. Both crews stepped with their coordination agreed.
texts.3: SP allowed a minimum of five minutes for the crew briefings and confirmed that each crew had covered inter-cockpit responsibilities, emergency procedures and crew coordination. The time was built into the briefing schedule rather than taken from the end of it, and no crew stepped with an item outstanding. The formation departed on schedule.
texts.4: SP managed the crew briefing period to an exceptional standard, protecting more than the five minute minimum within a briefing that still finished on time and directing the crews to the coordination points that the specific profile would stress. Each crew reported back the transfer of control and the emergency responsibilities it had agreed. No inter-cockpit responsibility was left to be settled airborne.
texts.marginal: SP allowed the five minute minimum for the crew briefings within standards, but the period was taken from the end of a session that had already slipped, and one crew used it to complete personal equipment rather than to brief coordination. The trend is toward a crew briefing period that is granted in form but not used for its purpose. SP is expected to schedule the period and to confirm what each crew covered in it on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP scheduled the crew briefing period with the IP directing that additional time be granted for the outstanding items. Protecting a full crew briefing period within the schedule is a first exposure at this stage, so the time is not yet allowed without a cue. The Training Section still expects IP assistance for this maneuver at this point. SP is expected to schedule the period and confirm what each crew covered in it.
texts_at.1: SP, due to about two minutes allowed for the crew briefings against the five required as a minimum, left the emergency procedures and crew coordination items uncovered in one cockpit until additional time was granted on direction, meeting the standard at the edge of what that extra time allowed. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to schedule the period and confirm what each crew covered in it.
texts_at.2: SP, due to a move to release the formation without calling the crew briefing period, recognized before the members left the room that no time had been set aside, calling the period, allowing the full five minutes and confirming coverage without prompting. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to schedule the period and confirm what each crew covered in it.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief delay before the crew briefing period was called, allowed a minimum of five minutes for the crew briefings and confirmed that each crew had covered inter-cockpit responsibilities, emergency procedures and crew coordination. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to schedule the period and confirm what each crew covered in it.

texts_above.1: SP allowed the crew briefing period, granting the additional time for the outstanding coordination items after it was directed by the IP. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus.
texts_above.2: SP moved to release the formation without calling the crew briefing period at first before recognizing before the members left the room that no time had been set aside, calling the period and confirming coverage without prompting. Building the crew briefing period into the schedule from the start would remove that late recognition. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to good crew-briefing time protection.
texts_above.3: SP allowed a minimum of five minutes for the crew briefings and confirmed that each crew had covered inter-cockpit responsibilities, emergency procedures and crew coordination, with the time built into the schedule rather than taken from its end. The period is already protected within the schedule; only the smallest further margin remains. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to very good crew-briefing time protection.
texts_above.4: SP protected more than the five minute minimum within a briefing that still finished on time, directing the crews to the coordination points the specific profile would stress and confirming the transfer of control each crew had agreed. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to excellent crew-briefing time protection.

error_modes.label: MISSION SPECIFIC STUDY AND CHAIR FLYING BEFORE THE BRIEFING

texts.0: SP, due to omitting the mission specific study before the sortie, arrived at the briefing without having reviewed the manoeuvres to be flown in the flight manual and this manual and without having chair flown the profile. The entry parameters for the rejoin and for the pitchout could not be stated when asked, and the local area procedures for the working area were unknown. IP had to stop the process and send SP to study before the briefing could continue.
texts.1: SP, due to study limited to reading the profile the evening before, could state the sequence of manoeuvres but not the entry parameters for two of them, and had not chair flown the sortie. The parameters were established only after IP directed SP to the relevant sections in turn, and the daily study topic was left uncovered. Preparation reached the lower limit of the standard through that prompting.
texts.2: SP, due to study focused on the primary mission with no time given to the alternate, could not initially state the profile that would be flown if the working area were unavailable. SP recognized the gap while reviewing the operational restrictions before the briefing, covered the alternate profile and chair flew its two unfamiliar manoeuvres, without IP intervention. Both lines of execution could then be briefed from memory.
texts.3: SP completed the mission specific study before the briefing. The manoeuvres to be flown had been reviewed in the flight manual and in this manual, the approach plates, operational restrictions and local area procedures had been covered, and the sortie had been chair flown with the checklists and specific tasks mentally reviewed. The daily study topic was covered and time had been given to the possible alternate mission.
texts.4: SP prepared to an exceptional standard, chair flying the whole profile including the alternate line of execution and visualizing each manoeuvre with its entry parameters, its checklist actions and the calls associated with it. Every parameter asked for during the briefing was stated from memory and referred to its source. The preparation removed any need to work out a procedure for the first time airborne.
texts.marginal: SP completed the mission specific study within standards, but the review of the manoeuvres was limited to this manual without the corresponding flight manual sections, and the chair flying covered the sequence without the checklist actions inside it. The trend is toward preparation that recalls what comes next without rehearsing how it is flown. SP is expected to chair fly the checklists and specific tasks together with the manoeuvre sequence on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP prepared for the mission with the IP directing the sections of the flight manual and this manual still to be reviewed. Completing the mission specific study without a directed section is a first exposure at this stage, so the preparation is not yet complete without a cue. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to chair fly the checklists and specific tasks together with the manoeuvre sequence.
texts_at.1: SP, due to study limited to reading the profile the evening before, stated the entry parameters for two manoeuvres only after being directed to the relevant sections in turn, with preparation meeting the standard at the edge of that prompting. Performance remained inside the standard required for this stage of training. SP is expected to chair fly the checklists and specific tasks together with the manoeuvre sequence.
texts_at.2: SP, due to study focused on the primary mission with no time given to the alternate, could not initially state the profile for an unavailable working area before recognizing the gap while reviewing the operational restrictions, covering the alternate profile and chair flying its unfamiliar manoeuvres without prompting. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to chair fly the checklists and specific tasks together with the manoeuvre sequence.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief gap before the alternate profile was chair flown, completed the mission specific study before the briefing, reviewing the manoeuvres in the flight manual and this manual and chair flying the sortie with checklists and specific tasks mentally reviewed. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to chair fly the checklists and specific tasks together with the manoeuvre sequence.

texts_above.1: SP completed the mission specific study, establishing the entry parameters for the two manoeuvres after being directed by the IP to the relevant sections. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP needed a review of the operational restrictions to close a gap in the profile for an unavailable working area, then covered the alternate profile and chair flew its two unfamiliar manoeuvres, without prompting. Covering the alternate during the first pass of study, rather than after the gap appears, would remove that addition. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to sound pre-briefing study depth.
texts_above.3: SP completed the mission specific study before the briefing, reviewing the manoeuvres in the flight manual and this manual and chair flying the sortie with the checklists and specific tasks mentally reviewed, with the daily study topic covered. The study already covers the primary and the alternate profile; only the smallest further margin remains. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to sure-handed pre-briefing study depth.
texts_above.4: SP chair flew the whole profile including the alternate line of execution, visualizing each manoeuvre with its entry parameters, checklist actions and calls, and stated every parameter asked for during the briefing from memory. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exceptional pre-briefing study depth.

error_modes.label: ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS AND DEPTH OF RECONSTRUCTION IN THE DEBRIEFING

texts.0: SP, as leader, debriefed the errors of the sortie without analysing their root causes and without stating how they would be corrected. The session was spent reconstructing the whole sortie event by event, including points that affected one cockpit only, and the time ran out with the two errors that affected the formation as a whole never analysed. IP had to conduct the analysis and produce the corrections.
texts.1: SP, as leader, named the errors observed but attributed them to their symptoms rather than to their causes, and offered no correction for any of them. The root cause of the two rejoin errors was reached only after IP directed the analysis step by step, and the corrections were supplied by IP. The debriefing met the lower limit of the standard through that intervention.
texts.2: SP, as leader, began the debriefing by reconstructing the sortie in detail from taxi onwards, including events that affected one aircraft only. SP recognized within the first minutes that the session would not reach the formation issues, cut the reconstruction to the detail needed to set up those issues and moved to the analysis of causes, without IP intervention. All formation level points were then covered with their corrections.
texts.3: SP analysed the root cause of each error and how it would be corrected, addressed all questions and concerns raised and emphasized the major learning points. The mission was reconstructed only in enough detail to debrief the issues that affected the formation as a whole. The session closed with each member holding a correction that could be applied on the next sortie.
texts.4: SP conducted an analysis of exceptional quality, tracing each error back through the events that produced it to a cause the crew could act on, and separating the causes that recurred across the sortie from single occurrences. Reconstruction was held to the minimum needed to establish each issue, and the corrections were stated in terms that can be measured on the next sortie. Every question raised was answered before the point was closed.
texts.marginal: SP analysed the causes of the errors and stated corrections within standards, but the reconstruction of the sortie occupied most of the session and two questions raised late were answered in outline only. The trend is toward a debriefing whose analysis is sound but is reached too late to be developed. SP is expected to limit reconstruction to the issues affecting the formation as a whole and to protect time for the questions on the next sortie.

texts_at.0: SP debriefed the sortie with the IP directing the analysis to the root cause of each rejoin error in turn. Reaching the root cause of an error without being directed step by step is a first exposure at this stage, so the analysis is not yet complete without a cue. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to limit reconstruction to the issues affecting the formation as a whole and protect time for the questions.
texts_at.1: SP, due to reconstruction of the sortie in detail from taxi onwards, including events that affected one aircraft only, reached the root cause of two rejoin errors only after each was directed step by step, with the debriefing meeting the standard through that direction. The result is in line with the proficiency expected at this point of the syllabus. SP is expected to limit reconstruction to the issues affecting the formation as a whole and protect time for the questions.
texts_at.2: SP, due to an opening that reconstructed the sortie in detail from taxi onwards, including single-cockpit events, recognized within the first minutes that the session would not reach the formation issues, cutting the reconstruction to the detail needed and moving to the analysis of causes without prompting. The standard for the Training Section was met. SP is expected to limit reconstruction to the issues affecting the formation as a whole and protect time for the questions.
texts_at.3: SP, due to a brief excess of reconstruction before the analysis of causes began, analysed the root cause of each error and how it would be corrected, addressing all questions raised and reconstructing the mission only in enough detail to debrief the formation-wide issues. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to limit reconstruction to the issues affecting the formation as a whole and protect time for the questions.

texts_above.2: SP reconstructed the sortie in detail from taxi onwards at first, including single-cockpit events, before recognizing within the first minutes that the session would not reach the formation issues, cutting the reconstruction and moving to the analysis of causes without prompting. Limiting reconstruction to formation-wide issues from the opening question would remove that early detour. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to solid debrief reconstruction-depth discipline.
texts_above.3: SP analysed the root cause of each error and how it would be corrected, addressing all questions raised and reconstructing the mission only in enough detail to debrief the issues affecting the formation as a whole. The reconstruction is already held to the formation-wide issues; only the smallest excess remains to trim. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to well-developed debrief reconstruction-depth discipline.
texts_above.4: SP traced each error back through the events that produced it to a cause the crew could act on, separated recurring causes from single occurrences and answered every question raised before closing the point. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to outstanding debrief reconstruction-depth discipline.
